topology: PC1 uses R1 as its gateway to independent TAC1 and RAD1 server LANs. Both prepared remote servers contain netadmin only; rescue exists only locally on R1.
implemented: Second ENCOR Security entry with accurate two-lab count; ENCOR now has34 labs. Existing CCNA local, TACACS+ and RADIUS exercises remain available.
Actual SSH logins distinguish default local authentication before a named list exists from a defined but unbound VTY-AUTH list; explicit line binding is required.

Named TACACS+ and RADIUS groups use real simulated TCP49 and UDP1812 authentication. Both remote netadmin and local rescue enter user EXEC at privilege1 because EXEC authorization is intentionally absent; a separate enable secret controls privileged EXEC.
An incorrect remote password and a valid local rescue credential both receive authoritative TACACS+ Reject while the primary is healthy; no later RADIUS or local method is attempted.

Disabling only TACACS+ permits RADIUS netadmin authentication; RADIUS Reject must still stop before local. Disabling both services permits rescue local fallback only after actual errors/retries. Fresh server echo replies prove preserved IP reachability.

Independent named CONSOLE local recovery requires a real fresh console login while both services are disabled. AAA console logout now clears identity and privilege, waits for Return and restarts the configured authentication, matching the protected line/local console flow.

Temporarily reversing the list requires an actual RADIUS-first login followed by restored TACACS+-first authentication. A wrong TACACS+ shared key produces a protocol error and RADIUS fallback; repairing it requires a fresh healthy primary login.

Authentication observations correlate immutable list definitions, method outcomes, server service/power/interface/key-match booleans, actual packet transaction IDs and server acceptance. No passwords or shared keys are added to observation metadata. History is bounded256 per device runtime.

Final save requires restored services, matching keys, the original method order and line bindings, all sixteen SSH-only VTYs with five-minute idle timeout, no active remote sessions, healthy planned addressing/links and R1 startup equality.

Practice starts0/20. Completed reference contains seven live configuration tasks without invented login, fault or packet evidence. Actual observations survive portable save as earned achievements; runtime sessions, traces and receiver state clear.
Diagnostic test aaa requests and generic log text alone cannot earn authenticated-session goals; unknown imported criteria, foreign roots and missing teaching interfaces fail closed.
scope: Authentication-focused IOS exercise. EXEC/command authorization and accounting are intentionally unconfigured; no UDP1813 or TACACS+ accounting records are invented. Separate existing AAA client labs exercise those features.
Primary Cisco documentation reviewed. No new live CML capture was performed for this catalog addition; existing CML AAA contracts are included in the full regression suite.
Shared-key protection, AAA wire formats, SSH cryptography and stored IOS secrets are logical teaching models, not external protocol interoperability.

Server service toggles are exercised through the normal Services AAA forms. Client statistics and packet events expose authentication activity; the existing server AAA log panel displays accounting records and remains empty in this lab.
Terminal styling, UI theme, layout and node artwork are unchanged.
